children: The FDA granted accelerated approval for RYBREVANT FASPRO as a single agent for adults with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC after platinum-based chemotherapy and anti–PD–(L)1 therapy, excluding HPV-associated OPSCC. Continued approval may depend on confirmation of clinical benefit.
FDA grants accelerated approval for HNSCC
Expands the drug's approved use beyond lung cancer, creating a new commercial indication; approval is accelerated and contingent on confirmatory evidence.
The approval rests on a relatively small early-phase cohort, making confirmation of benefit important to the durability of the indication.
Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 6% of patients
Serious safety risks could affect uptake and the product's risk-benefit assessment.

This is an early commercial expansion of an existing oncology drug into a new cancer indication, rather than a first approval for the product. A larger catalyst would require confirmatory Phase 3 OrigAMI-5 results verifying clinical benefit and evidence of commercial adoption.
